# @fluid-internal/mocha-test-setup

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->

**IMPORTANT: Fluid Framework uses this package as an implementation detail.**
**Do not use it as a public dependency.**
**We do not guarantee the stability of this package or its APIs.**

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->
<!-- markdown-magic:end -->

This package has a few main purposes:

-   Expose/generate a default `.mocharc.cjs` configuration for running [mocha](https://mochajs.org) tests, which other
    packages can extend.
-   Add mocha `beforeAll`, `beforeEach` and `afterEach` [root hook plugins](https://mochajs.org/#root-hook-plugins) to add
    some special behavior when we run tests.

## Running tests

For packages using this configuration, build the package and its tests, then run `pnpm exec mocha` from the package directory.

- [Select test files with `MOCHA_SPEC`](#mocha_spec).
- [Filter test names with Mocha's `--fgrep` or `--grep`](https://mochajs.org/running/cli/#--fgrep-string--f-string).
- [Enable performance measurements with `FLUID_TEST_PERF_MODE`](#fluid_test_perf_mode).

## Environment Variables

Set environment variables before running Mocha.
For cross-platform scripts, use `cross-env`, for example `pnpm exec cross-env MOCHA_SPEC=lib/test/example.spec.js mocha`.

### MOCHA_SPEC

Sets the compiled test file, directory, or glob to load, relative to the package directory.
It replaces the default selection of `lib/test` (or `dist/test` with [`FLUID_TEST_MODULE_SYSTEM=CJS`](#fluid_test_module_system)).
Unlike `MOCHA_SPEC`, positional file arguments and `--spec` add to the configured selection because of [Mocha's configuration merging](https://mochajs.org/next/running/configuring/#merging).
Name filtering alone still loads all configured test files; use `MOCHA_SPEC` to avoid loading unrelated files.

### FLUID_TEST_PERF_MODE

Set to `1` to measure benchmarks instead of running them as correctness tests.
Leave unset for correctness testing; do not use `0` to disable it.

This selects the benchmark reporter, sets a 1,000-second timeout per test, and writes results to `./benchmarkOutput.json`.
Override the timeout with [`FLUID_TEST_TIMEOUT`](#fluid_test_timeout) and the report path with `--reporterOptions reportFile=<path>`.

The default `@Benchmark` filter is omitted when you supply `--fgrep <text>` or `--grep <pattern>` (use these long options with separate arguments).
Your filter replaces, rather than intersects with, the default.
See [benchmark filtering](../../../tools/benchmark/README.md#--fgrep-benchmark) for tags and combining constraints.

### FLUID_TEST_TIMEOUT

Overrides Mocha's per-test timeout in milliseconds, including the performance-mode default.

### FLUID_TEST_FORBID_ONLY

When present, enables Mocha's `forbid-only` option to reject exclusive tests.

### FLUID_TEST_MODULE_SYSTEM

When set to "CJS", current run is setup to be for CommonJS coverage:
- "CJS" is noted as a variant and shown as prefix to test case names.
- The JUnit test-results file will be prefixed with "CJS-".
- Default spec is changed from `lib/test` to `dist/test`.

### FLUID_LOGGER_PROPS

Sets a JSON object serialized into the `testEnvProps` telemetry field.
Its `hostName` property also overrides the event's `hostName`:

```
FLUID_LOGGER_PROPS='{ "hostName": "Benchmark" }'
```

### FLUID_TEST_LOGGER_PKG_SPECIFIER

Specifies a module exporting `createTestLogger`, which returns an `ITelemetryBufferedLogger`.
The setup calls this factory, wraps the logger with test context, and installs the global `getTestLogger` function.
Use this variable rather than `--require` to configure a custom logger.
Pipelines use it to send telemetry to internal engineering systems.

## Base `mocharc.cjs` configuration

To leverage the base mocha configuration exposed by this package, first add it as a `devDependency` to your `package.json`
(the rest of the file has been omitted):

```json
{
	"devDependencies": {
		"@fluid-internal/mocha-test-setup": "version-that-matches-the-rest-of-the-release-group"
	}
}
```

Then put this in a `.mocharc.cjs` file at the root of your package:

```javascript
"use strict";

const getFluidTestMochaConfig = require("@fluid-internal/mocha-test-setup/mocharc-common");

const config = getFluidTestMochaConfig(__dirname);
module.exports = config;
```

If you need extra configuration, make changes to the `config` object before assigning it to `module.exports`.

Mocha will use this file by default if no path to a configuration file is provided explicitly.

The following excerpt shows some of the settings generated by `getFluidTestMochaConfig()`:

```jsonc
{
  "recursive": true,
  "require": ["@fluid-internal/mocha-test-setup", "source-map-support/register"], // can be extended by providing additionalRequiredModules to getFluidTestMochaConfig()
  "unhandled-rejections": "strict",
  "node-option": ["conditions=allow-ff-test-exports", "expose-gc"],
  "ignore": [ "**/*.tool.{js,cjs,mjs}" ], // Ignore "tools" which are scripts intended to be run, not part of the test suite.
  "spec": "lib/test" // Defaults to "lib/test" where esm tests typically are. Can be overridden via MOCHA_SPEC.
};
```

It is recommended that the source for tests files use a file name ending in ".spec.ts", but this is not enforced:
no file named based filtering of test files is done by default, except for the ignoring of `"**/*.tool.{js,cjs,mjs}"` noted above.

Note: some packages do explicitly filter test files to `*.spec.js`: in such packages test files with other names will be silently ignored.

## Special behavior

### Suppress console output by default

`console.log()`, `console.warn()` and `console.error()` are suppressed during tests unless `FLUID_TEST_VERBOSE` is set, for example `FLUID_TEST_VERBOSE=1`.

### Telemetry events

A couple of telemetry events `fluid:telemetry:Test_start` and `fluid:telemetry:Test_end` will be generated for each test.
The `Test_end` event includes fields with the test's state (passing/failed), its duration, if it timed out.
If a `FLUID_TEST_VARIANT` environment variable exists, the `testVariant` field in the events will have its value.
